observedSigns: Dark, sunken, leathery spots on the bottom of tomato fruits
possibleCauses: Blossom End Rot (often associated with calcium deficiency or irregular watering)
followUpQuestions: Are these spots appearing on the bottom (blossom end) of the fruit only, or are they also on the sides or top?
How often are you watering your plants?
Are you seeing these symptoms on all plants or just a few?
Have you noticed any wilting of the leaves during the hottest part of the day?
immediateActions: Ensure consistent watering to keep the soil moisture level steady, avoiding both waterlogging and extreme drying out.
Remove the affected fruits from the plant to allow the plant to focus energy on healthy fruit development.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer application, as this can interfere with calcium uptake.
Mulch around the base of the plants to help maintain consistent soil moisture.
assessment.whenToSeekHelp: If the spots continue to spread to new fruits despite consistent watering, or if you notice lesions on the leaves and stems, please consult your local agricultural extension worker for a professional field assessment.

uncertainty.reason: While the description strongly suggests Blossom End Rot, a definitive diagnosis cannot be made without visual confirmation of the fruit and an assessment of soil conditions.
